prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Defer Account Sign-In After Pet Selection [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +15.0%, measured -7.3% (p=0.004373), lost: worse
- round 1: Redesign Home Intro with Interactive Desktop Checklist [finish, redesign]: predicted +10.0%, measured +8.6% (p=0.05575), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Spotlight Layout for Path Selection [choose_path, layout]: predicted +8.0%, measured -2.0% (p=0.321988), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Desktop Display Overlay Troubleshooter Hint [home, hint]: predicted +5.0%, measured +0.7% (p=0.787796), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Desktop Controls & Tray Access Callout Hint [finish, hint]: predicted +2.5%, measured +2.1% (p=0.705743), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Clear Path Outcome Copy Optimization [choose_path, copy]: predicted +1.5%, measured -6.6% (p=0.00187), lost: worse
- round 2: Custom Pet Generation Status Indicator [adoption, wait_info]: predicted +14.0%, measured +14.7% (p=0.000155), won, confirmed by re-test
- round 3: Sign In Account Restoration Notice Layout [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +2.0%, measured +2.4% (p=0.324499), lost: no clear effect
- round 3: Story Onboarding Value Proposition Refinement [choose_path, copy]: predicted -4.0%, measured -0.3% (p=0.895535), lost: no clear effect
- round 3: Live Desktop Render Diagnostic Screen [home, new_screen]: predicted +3.5%, measured +6.1% (p=0.020897), won, confirmed by re-test

Previous lessons:
Adding a custom pet generation status indicator was helpful (+14.7% measured), and the prediction (+14.0%) was slightly too low.
Deferring account sign-in after pet selection significantly harmed performance (-7.3%), and the prediction (+15.0%) was far too high.
Path outcome copy optimization significantly harmed performance (-6.6%), and the prediction (+1.5%) was too high.
Desktop hints and callout overlays showed no clear effect; predictions (+2.5% to +5.0%) were too high.
Home intro redesigns (interactive checklist) and path layout changes (spotlight layout) showed no clear effect, and predictions (+8.0% to +10.0%) were too high.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Adding status indicators for wait steps (+14.7% measured) and diagnostic screens (+6.1% measured) were helpful; predictions (+14.0% and +3.5%) were slightly too low.
Deferring account sign-in significantly harmed performance (-7.3%), and the prediction (+15.0%) was far too high.
Path outcome copy optimization significantly harmed performance (-6.6%), and other copy refinements showed no clear effect; predictions were too high.
Desktop hints, callout overlays, intro redesigns, and layout changes showed no clear effect; predictions (+2.5% to +10.0%) were too high.
